page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC processor. Utilizing the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The processor is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

The server is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided by a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance via stress-ng, placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core performance is strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU tests. Memory bandwidth and database operations perform within the average range. This hardware profile is highly suited for compute-intensive workloads, software compilation, ray tracing, and text processing tasks.
description: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-500s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory, powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor running at 2.0 GHz. The architecture includes 16 physical cores with hyper-threading, supported by 32 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. Storage is provided by a bundled 500 GB NVMe SSD. In benchmark testing, the instance delivers top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities, ranking in the top 25% for software compilation, ray tracing, and PassMark CPU evaluations. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads, making it well-suited for software development pipelines, text processing, and parallelized compute tasks.
